svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.8.7.2 Continuity of Handrails
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.8 STAIRS, RAMPS, LANDINGS, HANDRAILS AND GUARDS
Continuity of Handrails

g.text: Outside a dwelling unit: one required handrail
Single dwelling unit: may start at
a newel post on the bottom tread

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Required handrails are continuously graspable
throughout the length of ramps, and of flights
of stairs from the bottom riser to the top
riser
Except as provided in Sentence (3).
At least one required handrail is continuous
throughout the length of the stair or ramp,
including at the landing, except where
interrupted by doorways
Except for stairs or ramps serving a single
dwelling unit or a house with a secondary suite.
Serving a single dwelling unit or a house with
a secondary suite, a handrail may start from a
newel post or volute installed on the bottom
tread
Why
Guidance and support matter most at the start and
end of ramps and flights, and at changes in
direction such as landings and winders. In a
single dwelling unit the handrail may stop at
landings.
Drawn: a two-flight stair outside a dwelling unit (left), and a dwelling stair with a newel post (right).
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.8.7.2. (page 9-36), with Note A-9.8.7.2.
